names_aka: electrophoretic lacquering / e-coating / ED clear coat (cataphoretic clear, 'electro-lacquer' in the jewelry trade)
nano-ceramic sol-gel clear coat (silane/siloxane hybrid, 'ceramic coating')
spray/dip lacquer (acrylic incl. Incralac-class, nitrocellulose 'zapon' class, 1K/2K polyurethane)
PVD color-matched hard cap (ZrN/TiN gold-tone, DLC) — cross-ref sibling PVD files
chromate passivate (HISTORICAL for this shop — Cr(VI) hazard)
principle: Everything in this family happens AFTER the gold (or gold-look) layer exists and attacks the two failure modes plating alone cannot fix: (1) CORROSION AT PINHOLES/WEAR-THROUGH — thin gold over Ni/steel is cathodic to its own defects, so the base corrodes preferentially at every pore; a molecular inhibitor film (BTA/thiol chemisorbed monolayer) or a continuous dielectric barrier (lacquer/e-coat/sol-gel, 2-25 um) seals the pores; (2) SCRATCH/WEAR — soft 24k-class gold (60-90 HV) is protected either by putting a sacrificial-but-harder transparent polymer/ceramic skin OVER it, or by putting the hardness UNDER/INSTEAD of it (hard interlayer, PVD nitride cap) — the full scratch-resistance ladder is ranked in deposit_properties. E-coat is the family's precision tool: the rinsed part is made an electrode in a waterborne polymer emulsion, DC field electro-deposits a self-limiting uniform film even in recesses (same throwing-power virtue as electroless Ni, but for lacquer), then oven-cure crosslinks it [FACT: mechanism]. Trade-off theme running through the whole file: every organic topcoat buys tarnish/scratch protection by trading away some 'bare noble metal' look/feel and adding a cure step and an aging/yellowing clock.

substrates: any FINISHED plated stack from the sibling files: electroplated Au on steel wire, PVD Au/nitride, ENIG-metallized ware
silver and silver-plated (the historic anti-tarnish customer — Ag sulfidizes; gold itself does NOT tarnish [FACT])
houseware: glass/ceramic already metallized (lacquer classes sized for large cm2)
NOT for: unplated bare steel (that is rust-proofing paint territory, different spec), food-CONTACT surfaces unless the specific coating carries food-contact clearance (see non_conductive_notes)
applicability.steel_wire_notes: For the anchor product (gold-plated steel-wire rings) the decision is SEQUENCE-CRITICAL: topcoats are applied to the FORMED, FINISHED piece — never coat-then-bend (all topcoats here crack or craze at wire-forming strains; e-coat acrylics tolerate the least handling flex of the premium options, waxes the most but protect the least). Wire-specific wins: (a) e-coat covers the cut ends and contact-point flats where gold is thinnest — exactly where a ring fails first; (b) a 5-15 um e-coat lets an economically thin gold layer (0.25-0.5 um) wear like a thicker one for low-abrasion SKUs, the standard fashion-jewelry cost play [FACT: industry practice]; (c) EN 1811 nickel-release: an intact continuous topcoat suppresses Ni release, BUT EU compliance must survive EN 12472 simulated wear+corrosion of the coating — a lacquer is not a legal substitute for a proper barrier/thickness stack [FACT: regulation structure].
applicability.non_conductive_notes: Houseware split by surface: OUTSIDE/décor surfaces of gilded cups, glass, spoon handles → lacquer/e-coat/sol-gel freely (e-coat needs the metallized layer live and conductive — it is an electro-process; sol-gel and spray lacquer do not care about conductivity). FOOD-CONTACT surfaces (bowl of spoon, cup lip/interior): default position is NO organic topcoat — leave honest, adequately thick gold bare; gold is the traditional food-safe gilding metal [FACT: historical/toxicological consensus] while migration clearance of a given lacquer for food contact is product-specific paperwork (FDA 21 CFR 175.300-class / EU framework 1935/2004-class for coatings) [UNKNOWN — needs coating supplier food-contact declaration per market]. Thiol/BTA molecular films on a drinking lip: no clearance, do not use [ESTIMATE: regulatory-conservative, high]. Dishwasher: assume NO topcoated gilded ware survives dishwashing regardless of coating claims — hand-wash care card [ESTIMATE: trade experience, high].
applicability.jewelry_thickness_classes: Topcoats do not change the GOLD class (ASTM B488 / ISO 27874 thickness classes are gold-layer classes) but they change which class you can get away with: flash (0.05-0.175 um) + 10 um e-coat = viable low-tier costume SKU; 'gold plated' 0.5-1 um + topcoat = mid tier; micron-class 2.5 um hard gold typically sold UNcoated (premium 'real metal touch') with only a molecular anti-tarnish/wax [FACT: market practice pattern]. Topcoat film classes themselves: molecular (nm, invisible), wax (sub-um), sol-gel 2-10 um, e-coat 5-25 um, spray lacquer 10-40 um.

components.name: final-clean station (ultrasonic DI + IPA vapor/wipe, tack-off)
components.purpose: topcoat adhesion dies on fingerprints, buffing compound and silicone; the part must be water-break-free AND dust-free
components.diy_notes: ultrasonic jewelry cleaner + 99% IPA + lint-free wipes + nitrile gloves from here to cure; ban ALL silicone products (mold release, polish, lubricants) from the room — one aerosol burst = fisheyes for weeks

components.name: anti-tarnish dip tank (0.5-2 L)
components.purpose: hold BTA or proprietary thiol passivate; 30-120 s dip is the whole process
components.diy_notes: lidded glass/PP; room temp; cheapest station in the entire factory

components.name: e-coat cell: tank + DC power supply 0-150 V + cathode/anode counter-electrode + stirrer
components.purpose: electro-deposit the waterborne clear; NOTE the supply is a VOLTAGE-mode unit (30-120 V, low current), NOT the plating rectifier (low-V high-A) — different instrument
components.diy_notes: jewelry-trade benchtop e-coat kits (1-5 L, gold- and clear-lacquer versions) are a mature hobby/small-shop product; a lab supply 150 V/1 A covers it; stainless counter-electrode; gentle magnetic stir

components.name: post-e-coat rinse (DI; industrial lines use ultrafiltrate/permeate rinse)
components.purpose: rinse off cream-like undeposited emulsion without scarring the soft wet film; industry closes the loop with UF to recover paint
components.diy_notes: at DIY scale: brief gentle DI rinse, accept the drag-out loss; no UF

components.name: cure oven, convection, 100-200 C, +/-5 C, DEDICATED (never a food oven)
components.purpose: crosslink e-coat (120-180 C class) and thermal sol-gel (150-250 C class); undercure = soft/solvent-weak film, overcure = yellowing/embrittlement
components.diy_notes: benchtop convection/toaster-class oven with a separate oven thermometer; steel wire substrate shrugs off 200 C, but check STONES/adhesives/plastic elements first — cure temperature is the compatibility gate for assembled jewelry

components.name: UV-cure unit (365-405 nm LED flood or conveyor)
components.purpose: cure UV-acrylate clears in seconds at room temperature — the route when the piece cannot take oven heat
components.diy_notes: nail-lamp-class LED units genuinely work for small pieces; oxygen inhibition leaves a tacky surface skin — cure in N2, or use a wax-additive formula, or accept a wipe-down step

components.name: spray station: airbrush/HVLP mini-gun + extracted booth (or dip-and-drain rig)
components.purpose: apply solvent/UV lacquers on houseware-scale cm2 where e-coat tank size is the limit
components.diy_notes: airbrush 0.3-0.5 mm at 1-2 bar for jewelry; dip-and-drain with a slow motorized withdrawal (1-5 mm/s) gives surprisingly uniform lacquer on cups/spoons; SOLVENT SPRAY NEEDS REAL EXTRACTION + no ignition sources [FACT: flammability]

components.name: rack/jig with minimal-contact hooks
components.purpose: every contact point is a bare spot in e-coat and a run-nucleus in lacquer
components.diy_notes: hang rings on thin SS wire through the bore at the future solder/hidden point; plan the touch point at the least-visible spot — this decision is cosmetic yield

components.name: dust management: covered flash-off shelf, HEPA-ish cabinet or simple lidded tote
components.purpose: wet lacquer is a dust magnet during flash-off; dust nibs are the #1 cosmetic reject
components.diy_notes: a clear plastic tote over the drying rack removes most of the problem for free

components.name: test bench: pencil-hardness set, cross-hatch cutter + tape, MEK/IPA rub cloth, crockmeter-improvised rub jig
components.purpose: coating QC is cheap and fast — use it every batch
components.diy_notes: full pencil set (6B-9H) costs little; cross-hatch can be a razor + defined spacing jig

components.name: strip/rework station (solvent or alkaline paint stripper compatible with gold)
components.purpose: reject topcoats must come OFF without eating the gold — gold is inert to organic solvents, so acetone/NMP-free-class strippers or hot alkaline strippers work; PVD nitride caps are NOT strippable at DIY (re-plate route instead)
components.diy_notes: acetone soak strips most uncured/1K lacquers; cured e-coat/2K needs commercial stripper + patience; test on a coupon first

operation_sequence.action: GATE: only accept parts that already passed the plating acceptance tests (thickness/adhesion/color) — a topcoat hides defects from the eye, not from failure; forming/assembly must be COMPLETE (topcoat is the last chemical step)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: topcoating a part with plating adhesion problems laminates the failure in — it will blister as one piece later

operation_sequence.action: final clean: ultrasonic DI detergent-free, DI rinse, IPA rinse/wipe, dry warm filtered air; gloves-only handling from now on
operation_sequence.failure_watch: fingerprint = adhesion void + visible ghost under clear coat; buffing-compound residue in crevices = fisheyes and peel origins

operation_sequence.action: anti-tarnish dip (BTA for Cu/Ag-bearing surfaces, proprietary thiol passivate for general/Au-flash-over-Ni surfaces), drain, DI rinse per TDS (some no-rinse), warm-air dry
operation_sequence.parameters: RT-50 C, 30-120 s immersion, gentle motion
operation_sequence.failure_watch: over-concentration or no-rinse misuse = visible haze/iridescent film on the gold; thiol passivates: exceed dwell and wettability of a SUBSEQUENT topcoat drops (they are release-layer-like) — if e-coating after, confirm passivate/e-coat compatibility per TDS or skip the dip

operation_sequence.action: BRANCH A (jewelry precision route) — e-coat: immerse part live on the rack, apply DC, film self-limits, withdraw, gentle DI rinse
operation_sequence.parameters: bath 20-30 C, solids/pH per TDS (cathodic acrylic class: pH 5-6.5), 30-120 V DC ramped over ~5-10 s, 30-120 s total, target 5-15 um (jewelry) / 15-25 um (hardware class)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: gas bubbles pinned on complex geometry = craters (angle the part, stir); contact-point bare spot (plan it); film thickness rises with voltage/time until self-insulation — chasing thickness past the window causes rupture ('film burn') streaks

operation_sequence.action: BRANCH B (houseware/large-area or non-conductive-safe route) — sol-gel nano-ceramic or lacquer: dip-and-slow-withdraw, spray, or brush; flash-off solvent under dust cover
operation_sequence.parameters: sol-gel dip withdrawal 1-5 mm/s for 2-5 um/pass; spray lacquer 2-3 light coats, 5-15 min flash-off between; RH < 65% for solvent lacquers (moisture blush)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: runs/drips at drain edges (hang orientation, wick the drip point with a brush tip); white haze = humidity blush (re-flow with retarder thinner or re-do in drier air); orange peel = too-fast solvent or too-dry spray

operation_sequence.action: cure: e-coat and thermal sol-gel to oven; UV-acrylate to UV unit; air-dry lacquers to covered rack
operation_sequence.parameters: e-coat 120-180 C 15-30 min metal temperature (per TDS); thermal sol-gel 150-250 C 30-60 min class; UV 1-10 J/cm2 class; nitrocellulose/acrylic air-dry: dust-free in 10-30 min, full hardness days
operation_sequence.duration: 15-60 min (oven/UV) or 24-72 h to full properties (air-dry)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: undercure: fails MEK rub, blocks (sticks) in bags, soft pencil number; overcure/overtemp: yellow tint on a WHITE-metal look is instantly visible, on gold it reads as 'brassy' color shift; stones/glue joints: check max temperature BEFORE the batch

operation_sequence.action: optional final wax (carnauba/microcrystalline) buffed on handled décor pieces over or instead of lacquer
operation_sequence.failure_watch: wax on a surface that will later need lacquer/e-coat = guaranteed fisheyes; wax is always the LAST material to touch the part

operation_sequence.action: QC per testing_acceptance: visual under raking light, pencil hardness, cross-hatch+tape on a same-batch coupon, MEK/IPA double-rub for cure, batch-sample tarnish/sweat exposure; then pack in tarnish-inhibiting tissue/ziplock with desiccant
operation_sequence.failure_watch: packing warm/undercured parts in closed bags = blocking and solvent-trap haze; storage is part of the process (anti-tarnish paper, FIFO)

solutions.purpose: chemisorbed Cu-BTA (and Ag-azole) complex monolayer-to-nm film that blocks sulfide/oxide tarnish on Cu, brass, bronze, Ag and at Cu/Ni-exposing pores of thin gold; invisible, feel-free, near-zero cost; the classic museum/electronics inhibitor

composition.role: corrosion inhibitor — complexes surface Cu(I)/Ag(I) into an insoluble polymeric azole film [FACT: mechanism]
composition.hazard_class: Acute Tox. 4 (oral), eye irritant, harmful to aquatic life w/ long-lasting effects class [FACT]

composition.chemical: solvent/carrier: DI water, or water/IPA blend for faster dry
composition.role: carrier; IPA improves wetting and flash-off on jewelry
BTA homolog, better high-temp persistence; interchangeable at this scale

operating_window.temperature_C: 15-50 (warm speeds film formation) [FACT: published typical range]
operating_window.pH: 5-8 as-dissolved; no adjustment normally needed [FACT: published practice]
operating_window.deposition_rate: film complete in 30-120 s; nm-scale, self-limiting [FACT: published]

solutions.maintenance: Bath is stable for months lidded; replenish on volume loss; discard on visible contamination. Carry-over: rinse (or drip-dry per TDS) before any SUBSEQUENT organic coating — azole films can reduce lacquer wet-out [ESTIMATE: practice-based, medium]. Spent bath: small-volume aquatic-relevant organic waste — collect, do not drain [FACT: hazard class].

solutions.solution_name: proprietary thiol/SAM 'nano' anti-tarnish passivate (chromate-free, the modern jewelry-trade dip)
solutions.purpose: self-assembled alkyl/aryl-thiol or phosphonate monolayer that bonds to Au/Ag/Ni/Cu surfaces, adds hydrophobicity and tarnish/sweat resistance without visible film — the standard 'anti-tarnish dip' sold to plating shops; also the DROP-IN REPLACEMENT for legacy Cr(VI) chromate passivates, which are Carc. 1A and excluded from this factory [FACT: Cr(VI) hazard class]

composition.role: monolayer former (S-Au and S-Ag affinity is the design basis [FACT: SAM chemistry])
composition.hazard_class: [UNKNOWN — needs supplier SDS; thiol class typically irritant/odorous]

composition.role: carrier
uniform wet-out on mixed-metal assemblies

operating_window.current_density_A_dm2: n/a (electrolytic-assist versions exist for silver — then per TDS)
operating_window.deposition_rate: monolayer in 30-90 s, self-limiting [FACT: SAM kinetics class]

solutions.maintenance: Bought made-up; life measured in work-throughput per TDS. KEY INTERACTION: a fresh SAM lowers surface energy — if the SKU also gets e-coat/lacquer, either verify overcoatability with the supplier or sequence the SAM as the FINAL step on no-lacquer SKUs only [ESTIMATE: practice-based, high]. Not for food-contact surfaces [ESTIMATE: regulatory-conservative, high].

solutions.solution_name: cathodic electrophoretic clear lacquer (e-coat / ED clear, acrylic-urethane waterborne class)
solutions.purpose: THE precision clear topcoat for jewelry: DC-driven self-limiting deposition of a waterborne polymer film that is uniform on complex shapes, edge-covering, thin-controllable (5-25 um), then oven-crosslinked; the mass-market mechanism behind long-lived fashion jewelry and 'tarnish-proof' gold flash; available tinted (gold-tone) for color-correcting pale flash [FACT: industry practice]

composition.chemical: acrylic / acrylic-urethane cationic resin emulsion (amine-solubilized, cathodic type)
composition.role: film former; cathodic (part = cathode) chosen because it does not anodically dissolve the plated metal — anodic e-coat on fresh gold/Ni risks substrate staining [FACT: cathodic-vs-anodic rationale]
composition.hazard_class: low acute hazard as emulsion; amine neutralizers irritant class [FACT: class-level]
composition.tag: [FACT: published class range for decorative ED clears]

composition.role: film coalescence and flow
keeps cationic resin dispersed; consumed/regenerated at electrodes — pH drift is the daily control

composition.chemical: crosslinker (blocked isocyanate or melamine class, latent until oven)
composition.role: unblocks at cure T and crosslinks — the reason the film's chemical/scratch resistance appears only AFTER full cure
composition.hazard_class: blocked isocyanates: respiratory sensitizer class ON CURE FUME; melamine-formaldehyde: formaldehyde release class on overbake [FACT: class-level]

composition.role: delays yellowing/embrittlement — ask for it explicitly; its absence is why cheap clear-coated jewelry ambers

operating_window.temperature_C: bath 20-30; cure 120-180 metal-temperature 15-30 min [FACT: published class ranges]
operating_window.pH: 5-6.5 (cathodic acrylic class); drifts in use, corrected per TDS [FACT: published class]
operating_window.current_density_A_dm2: current is a dependent variable — process is voltage-controlled; expect initial 0.1-1 A/dm2 decaying toward zero as film self-insulates [FACT: mechanism]
operating_window.voltage: 30-120 V DC, soft-start ramp 5-10 s (instant full V = film rupture); thickness tracks voltage+time to the self-limit [FACT: published class range]
operating_window.agitation: continuous gentle stir — emulsion settles; filter 25-50 um loop on larger tanks
operating_window.deposition_rate: 5-15 um in 30-120 s, then self-limiting; ONE pass only (a cured film is an insulator — no second e-coat) [FACT: mechanism]
operating_window.anode: counter-electrode stainless (anode in cathodic systems); inspect/clean — anode fouling shifts bath pH balance

solutions.maintenance: Buy as a paired system (emulsion + replenisher/solvent + pH corrector) and run by TDS: monitor solids (draw-down weight or supplier hydrometer method), pH, conductivity; replenish per amp-time or per surface-area throughput. Contamination killers: silicone (fisheyes forever — quarantine the room), plating-bath drag-in salts (conductivity spike = rough deposit — RINSE WELL after plating), microbial growth in idle warm bath (lid, biocide per TDS, or refrigerate small kits). Drag-out is unrecoverable at DIY scale; industrial UF-permeate rinse recovery exists [FACT: industry practice].

solutions.purpose: the SCRATCH-HARDNESS champion among wet-applied clears: hydrolyzed alkoxysilane network (organic-inorganic hybrid) gives glass-like pencil hardness (6H-9H class vs 1-3H for acrylic lacquers) in a thin 2-10 um film; dip/spray applicable on conductive or NON-conductive ware alike — the houseware wide-area tool; thermal- or UV-curable variants

composition.role: SiO2 backbone after hydrolysis/condensation — the hardness source
the 'hybrid' flexibilizer — pure SiO2 films crack above ~1 um; organic bridges allow 2-10 um crack-free and bond to metal/lacquer [FACT: hybrid sol-gel principle]

composition.typical_range: balance; H2O at r ≈ 2-4 mol per mol Si
composition.role: carrier + hydrolysis reagent; pot-life clock starts when water+catalyst meet the silanes
controls hydrolysis/condensation rate → pot life hours-to-days

composition.chemical: optional nano-filler (colloidal SiO2 10-30 nm) or commercial one-pack '9H ceramic' equivalents
composition.role: hardness/abrasion boost; commercial automotive-class 'ceramic coating' one-packs are this chemistry pre-packaged and are the sane DIY entry
composition.hazard_class: low (bound colloid; no free respirable silica in liquid) [FACT: class-level]

operating_window.temperature_C: apply 15-30; cure: thermal 150-250 C 30-60 min class, or 80-120 C extended for temperature-limited assemblies (lower hardness), UV-hybrid versions per TDS [FACT: published class ranges]
operating_window.pH: sol at pH 3-5 (acid route); not a controlled bath parameter after mixing — POT LIFE is the real variable (hours-days, gels irreversibly)
operating_window.agitation: n/a; dip-withdrawal speed IS the thickness control (1-5 mm/s ≈ 2-5 um class per pass) [FACT: dip-coating relation]
operating_window.deposition_rate: 2-5 um per dip pass; max ~10 um total before crack risk [FACT: published hybrid sol-gel limit class]

solutions.maintenance: Not a maintainable bath — a POT-LIFE mixture: mix small batches, log time-since-mix, discard at viscosity rise (gel point is sudden). Store silane precursors dry and sealed (they hydrolyze on air moisture). Commercial one-pack versions shift the pot-life burden to shelf-life — preferred at DIY scale. Waste: gelled sol is inert silica-organic solid, solvent-wet → dry then ordinary solid waste; liquid solvent waste to flammables collection [FACT: class-level].

solutions.solution_name: conventional lacquer classes for houseware (acrylic/Incralac-class, nitrocellulose, 1K/2K PU, UV-acrylate)
solutions.purpose: the wide-area, low-capex décor topcoats for gilded cups, trays, spoon HANDLES and display ware; selection = trade-off table: acrylic (reversible, museum-grade, moderate hardness), nitrocellulose (historic 'zapon' for gilt, fast, yellows, very flammable), 2K PU (toughest and most chemical-resistant, isocyanate hazard), UV-acrylate (fast, hard, needs UV unit)

composition.typical_range: 10-20 resin in solvent; BTA 0.5-3 of resin
composition.role: the reference metal-décor lacquer: clear, UV-stable, REVERSIBLE (acetone re-strip), built-in inhibitor [FACT: conservation-standard formulation class]
fast-dry classic; INCLUDED FOR COMPLETENESS, ranked LAST: yellows, embrittles, and the resin itself is a flammable-solid/energetic class material [FACT]
composition.hazard_class: highly flammable liquid AND film; dry NC is self-sustaining combustion class [FACT]

composition.chemical: 2K polyurethane clear (polyol part A + aliphatic polyisocyanate part B, HDI-trimer class)
composition.typical_range: mix per ratio; 30-50 solids as applied
composition.role: hardest-wearing organic clear short of sol-gel; aliphatic (HDI) type chosen for non-yellowing [FACT: coatings practice]
composition.hazard_class: ISOCYANATES: respiratory sensitizer Cat 1 — sensitization is permanent; spray application without supplied-air/serious LEV is out of bounds for a home shop [FACT]

composition.chemical: UV-curable acrylate clear (urethane-acrylate oligomer + reactive diluents + photoinitiator)
composition.role: seconds-cure hard clear for heat-sensitive assemblies; jewelry 'doming' resins are this class
composition.hazard_class: acrylate monomers: skin sensitizer/irritant class; photoinitiator low; UV source is an eye hazard [FACT]

operating_window.temperature_C: apply 18-25, RH < 65% (blush limit for solvent types); force-dry 50-60 C acceptable for acrylic/NC; 2K per TDS; UV cure at RT [FACT: coatings practice class]

operating_window.deposition_rate: 10-25 um dry film from 2-3 coats typical; 2K PU 25-40 um single-visit; UV 20-100 um per shot [FACT: class ranges]

solutions.maintenance: 1K lacquers: solvent make-up for viscosity (measure with a cheap flow cup), keep lidded, respect shelf life. 2K: POT LIFE 1-8 h after mixing — mix only what the batch needs; part-B (isocyanate) drums die on moisture ingress (CO2 + gel). UV resin: keep dark/lidded. Food-contact: NONE of these classes may be assumed food-safe as decorative grades — food-side surfaces stay uncoated gold, or demand the supplier's explicit food-contact-compliant grade + declaration [UNKNOWN — needs supplier food-contact declaration per market].

composition.role: reactive gas; color-matching to a retained gold standard is an iterative N2-flow tuning exercise [FACT: reactive-PVD practice]

composition.role: true-gold color/skin over the hard nitride; also the marketing/marking difference ('gold plated' claims need real Au at the surface) [FACT: marking-regulation structure]

operating_window.temperature_C: substrate 100-300 during deposition (below steel temper concerns, above many stones/adhesives — assembly compatibility gate) [FACT: published class]
operating_window.current_density_A_dm2: n/a — see sibling pvd_dc_magnetron_sputtering.json / pvd_evaporation_ion_plating.json for full parameter sets

solutions.maintenance: Per sibling PVD files. Decision-relevant here: nitride caps are NOT reworkable at DIY (no gentle strip); color-match tolerance vs electroplated gold on adjacent SKUs is a real merchandising problem (ZrN ≈ gold but not equal under all lighting) — keep PVD-capped and electroplated pieces out of the same matched set unless the top-flash variant is used [ESTIMATE: trade practice, high].

prep_chain_required: 1. FULL plating acceptance passed (thickness, adhesion, color per sibling files) — topcoats seal in whatever exists; WHY: a topcoat over failing plate laminates the defect and blisters as a unit.

2. ALL forming, cutting, soldering, tumbling, polishing, stone-setting COMPLETE — topcoat is the terminal chemical step; WHY: every topcoat here cracks at forming strains and any later hot-work destroys it.
3. Post-polish deep clean: ultrasonic DI (no oily soaps), DI rinse, IPA rinse, filtered warm dry; WHY: buffing compound and fingerprints are the #1 adhesion and fisheye cause.
4. Silicone quarantine of the finishing room (no silicone polish/spray/mold-release anywhere near); WHY: ppm airborne silicone = fisheye epidemics in e-coat and lacquer, near-impossible to purge.

5. If anti-tarnish dip AND organic topcoat are both specified: verify overcoatability (supplier compatibility statement) or apply the dip only to no-lacquer SKUs; WHY: SAM/azole films lower surface energy and can de-wet the topcoat.

6. For e-coat: extra-thorough DI rinse after plating (conductivity of carried-in salts disturbs the emulsion) and a planned, cosmetically hidden rack contact point; WHY: bath contamination and bare contact spots are e-coat's two systematic defects.
7. For cure-oven routes: batch-level max-temperature audit of every non-metal element (stones, adhesives, patina waxes); WHY: the coating cure window must fit the weakest component, not the wire.

deposit_properties.purity_karat: n/a — no gold is added by this family (except the optional PVD top-flash); the family's job is to PRESERVE the karat color underneath. Tinted 'gold-tone' e-coats and yellowed clears effectively ADULTERATE perceived color — spec water-clear, UV-stabilized grades for premium SKUs.
deposit_properties.hardness_HV: ranked scratch ladder (surface reads as the TOPMOST layer): bare soft gold 60-90 HV < hard acid gold 130-200 HV (sibling file) < acrylic/NC lacquer ≈ pencil HB-2H < e-coat acrylic-urethane ≈ 2H-4H < 2K PU ≈ 2-4H tougher-not-harder (best mar recovery) < sol-gel hybrid 6H-9H pencil class < ZrN/TiN 1500-2500 HV < DLC 2000-4000 HV [FACT: published class values; pencil and HV scales noted as non-interchangeable]. STRATEGY TRADE-OFFS: polymer clears are sacrificial (they take the scratch, polishable/re-strippable, but 'plastic' feel and aging clock); sol-gel is near-glass hard but thin and non-reworkable-in-place; PVD nitride is the durability ceiling but capex-heavy, non-strippable, color-match-imperfect; hard-gold-with-no-topcoat is the premium-honest option paying in gold thickness [FACT+ESTIMATE mix as tagged].
deposit_properties.thickness_per_pass: molecular passivates: nm, invisible; wax sub-um; sol-gel 2-5 um/dip (10 um total ceiling); e-coat 5-25 um single self-limiting pass; spray lacquer 5-12 um dry/coat, 2-3 coats; UV 20-100 um/shot; PVD cap 0.2-1 um.
deposit_properties.color_control: the family's color duties: (1) DO NO HARM — water-clear + UVA/HALS grades, cure inside window (overbake = amber shift on gold reads 'brassy', catastrophic on rhodium/silver-white SKUs); (2) COLOR-CORRECT — gold-tinted e-coat can pull a pale/thin flash toward rich yellow (industry trick; mark honestly); (3) COLOR-MATCH PVD — ZrN N2-flow tuning against a retained master under D65-class light; note polymer-coated vs bare-gold pieces differ in GLOSS even at identical hue — matched sets should share one finishing route [ESTIMATE: trade practice, high].
deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes: PLATE-THEN-FORM ANSWER, FAMILY-WIDE: topcoats are the LAST step, applied to the finished formed shape — full stop. Cured e-coat/2K films tolerate mild elastic flex of a finished ring in wear but NOT forming strains (crack, whiten, peel from the crack line); sol-gel is glass-brittle above ~1% strain class; PVD nitride caps craze exactly like the Ni-P case in the electroless file [FACT: brittle-film mechanics]. Corollary for the continuous-wire concept: an in-line anti-tarnish dip + wax on the moving wire is legitimate (molecular films flex), but any HARD topcoat must wait until after ring forming — i.e. the topcoat station lives at the END of the piece line, not on the wire line [ESTIMATE: engineering inference, high].

testing_acceptance.acceptance: meets the SKU's declared class (e-coat ≥2H, sol-gel ≥6H typical targets); tested on same-batch coupon after FULL cure schedule
4B-5B class (≤5% lattice lift); on wire pieces use bend-coupon proxy: no coating lift adjacent to a defined mild bend

testing_acceptance.standard_class: MEK (or IPA for acrylics) double-rub, ASTM D4752 class practice
testing_acceptance.acceptance: ≥50 double rubs without breakthrough for crosslinked systems; failure = undercure, re-bake if TDS allows

testing_acceptance.standard_class: thioacetamide / flowers-of-sulfur exposure, ISO 4538-class practice (Ag/Cu-bearing SKUs)
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no visible tarnish at coated pores vs uncoated control coupon at the SKU's declared exposure duration
no blistering, no under-film corrosion bloom, no color shift ΔE beyond retained-standard tolerance after 24-96 h class
hours-to-rating per SKU class; jewelry SKUs usually skip NSS for sweat/tarnish tests [ESTIMATE: practice, high]

testing_acceptance.standard_class: crockmeter/abrasive-rub count class; Taber for flatware
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no wear-through to under-layer at declared cycle count; define the endpoint as FIRST under-layer color read-through

testing_acceptance.test: nickel release AFTER simulated wear (EU skin-contact SKUs)
testing_acceptance.standard_class: EN 1811 preceded by EN 12472 wear+corrosion [FACT: regulation pairing]
testing_acceptance.acceptance: <0.5 ug/cm2/wk (articles) / <0.2 (piercing) — the coating must pass AFTER EN 12472, i.e. a lacquer alone is not a compliance strategy; send-out lab

testing_acceptance.standard_class: FDA 21 CFR 175.300-class / EU 1935/2004-framework testing via supplier declaration + lab
testing_acceptance.acceptance: [UNKNOWN — needs supplier food-contact declaration and per-market lab test; default design rule: food-side = bare gold, no organic coating]

testing_acceptance.standard_class: oven-aging (e.g. 80 C/7 d class) + ΔE vs retained standard; UV cabinet if available
testing_acceptance.acceptance: ΔE within house tolerance; grades without UVA/HALS expected to fail — screen before adopting any new clear [ESTIMATE: practice, high]
no fisheyes, dust nibs, runs, contact-point bare spots beyond hidden zone, orange peel per gloss class

defects_and_remedies.defect: fisheyes (circular craters/repelled dots in wet film)
defects_and_remedies.cause: silicone or oil contamination — on the part, in the air, in the booth line
defects_and_remedies.remedy: strip, re-clean with IPA, eliminate silicone source (quarantine the room); fisheye-eliminator additives exist but treat the symptom [FACT: coatings canon]

defects_and_remedies.defect: blistering days-to-weeks after coating, or on first hot-water contact
defects_and_remedies.cause: trapped rinse water/solvent under film (undercured, coated-wet crevices), or coating over failing plate adhesion
defects_and_remedies.remedy: full flash-off before cure, blow out crevices, bake schedule per TDS; if blister base shows plating — the reject belongs to the PLATING step, tighten the step-1 gate

defects_and_remedies.defect: yellow/amber shift of the clear coat
defects_and_remedies.cause: overbake, nitrocellulose or non-stabilized resin aging, UV exposure
defects_and_remedies.remedy: cure inside window with an oven thermometer; spec UVA/HALS-stabilized acrylic/PU grades; ban NC from premium SKUs; strip-and-recoat is possible for 1K acrylics (reversible) — the reason Incralac-class is the museum default

defects_and_remedies.defect: e-coat bare spot at rack contact
defects_and_remedies.cause: mechanism-intrinsic: no deposition where the contact touches
defects_and_remedies.remedy: design the contact at a hidden point (inside of ring shank), touch-up with brush lacquer, or double-hit rotation (re-rack on a different point and second short deposition BEFORE cure — wet film only)

defects_and_remedies.cause: plating-salt drag-in, dust, emulsion breakdown, microbial growth in idle bath
defects_and_remedies.remedy: harder DI rinsing upstream, filter loop, lid + biocide per TDS; badly contaminated small kits: dump and remake (kits are sized to make this cheap)

defects_and_remedies.cause: voltage too high or applied without soft-start ramp; local field concentration at sharp points
defects_and_remedies.remedy: ramp 5-10 s to setpoint, drop 10-20 V, orient sharp points away from the counter-electrode

defects_and_remedies.cause: humidity condensation during fast solvent flash (evaporative cooling) — RH too high
defects_and_remedies.remedy: coat under RH<65%, add retarder thinner, or gently re-flow with a slow solvent pass; sol-gel analog: hazy = premature gelation or over-aged sol — remix fresh

defects_and_remedies.defect: runs, drips, fat edges on dipped houseware
defects_and_remedies.cause: withdrawal too fast, viscosity too high, no drip-wicking
defects_and_remedies.remedy: slow motorized withdrawal 1-5 mm/s, thin per flow-cup spec, wick the drain point with a brush tip at flash-off

defects_and_remedies.defect: coating cracks/whitens when the piece is bent or sized
defects_and_remedies.cause: hard topcoat applied before forming — sequence violation
defects_and_remedies.remedy: none on the piece (strip and redo after forming); enforce 'topcoat last' routing; ring-sizing service on coated rings requires strip → size → recoat

defects_and_remedies.cause: oxygen inhibition of the surface layer
defects_and_remedies.remedy: cure under nitrogen blanket, use wax-additive formula, higher-irradiance final pass, or IPA wipe of the inhibited skin [FACT: UV-coatings canon]

defects_and_remedies.defect: tarnish appears UNDER an apparently intact clear coat
defects_and_remedies.cause: coat applied over already-contaminated/finger-printed surface, or pinholes in too-thin film wicking sweat
defects_and_remedies.remedy: clean-to-coat time discipline (same shift), minimum film build per class, add the anti-tarnish dip UNDER the coat where compatible (belt-and-suspenders on Ag/Cu-bearing stacks)
respect full-hardness times (air-dry lacquers need days), cool from oven before bagging, interleave tissue

defects_and_remedies.defect: gloss mismatch inside a matched set
defects_and_remedies.cause: mixed finishing routes (bare gold vs e-coat vs sol-gel) across pieces of one set
defects_and_remedies.remedy: one set = one topcoat route; keep retained masters per route and light-booth check

cost_drivers: capex tier is the family's headline: anti-tarnish dip ≈ tens-of-currency-units chemistry only; benchtop e-coat kit + 150 V supply + toaster-class oven = low hundreds; UV unit low hundreds; sol-gel one-packs cheap per piece but pot-life scrap; PVD cap inherits the sibling files' vacuum capex — the ladder lets the owner buy scratch resistance incrementally [ESTIMATE: class-level, no invented prices]
per-piece chemistry cost is trivial vs gold cost (um of polymer vs um of Au) — the REAL cost is the added process time: cure oven occupancy (15-60 min/batch) and air-dry days of WIP inventory
cosmetic yield: dust nibs and fisheyes are the yield tax; a lidded flash-off tote and silicone discipline are the cheapest yield investments in the whole factory
energy: cure oven is modest (small chamber, batched); nothing here rivals plating-bath heat loads
rework economics: 1K acrylic strip-and-recoat is cheap (acetone); cured e-coat/2K strip is slow labor; PVD cap rework = re-plate the part — reworkability is a hidden selection criterion
e-coat bath as slow consumable: solids deplete per cm2 throughput; small kits are priced as periodic full-replacement items
2K PU pot-life scrap: every mixed-but-unused gram is waste — batch discipline or switch that SKU to 1K/UV

testing: mostly pennies (pencils, tape, rub cloth); the exceptions are send-out EN 1811 (EU jewelry) and any food-contact migration testing — the latter is the single strongest argument for the 'food-side = bare gold, coat outside only' design rule

market side: 'anti-tarnish / scratch-resistant' claims raise price-point and cut returns — this family is cheap insurance on warranty/returns cost, the usual justification in fashion-jewelry economics [ESTIMATE: trade reasoning, medium]

hazards: 2K polyurethane isocyanate hardeners: respiratory sensitizer Cat 1 class — sensitization permanent; spray form is the worst exposure route [FACT]
UV-acrylate monomers: skin sensitizer/irritant class; UV lamps: eye/skin photohazard [FACT]
solvent lacquers and sol-gel carriers (ketones, esters, aromatics, alcohols): flammable liquid Cat 2-3, vapor explosion range in unventilated rooms; static ignition during spray [FACT]
nitrocellulose: highly flammable, dry film/overspray self-sustaining combustion class [FACT]
blocked-isocyanate/melamine e-coat crosslinkers: cure-oven fume carries respiratory-sensitizer/formaldehyde-class species on unblocking — vent the oven [FACT: class-level]
BTA/TTA: Acute Tox. 4 oral class, aquatic-chronic class [FACT]
legacy chromate passivates: Cr(VI) Carc. 1A — designated historical-prohibited in this factory; thiol/azole chemistry replaces them fully at this scale [FACT]
cure oven: burn hazard; NEVER a food oven (coating fume condensate) [FACT: basic hygiene rule]
e-coat electricals: 30-120 V DC in an aqueous tank — above the plating line's touch-safe voltages; interlock/insulate rack handling [FACT: electrical class]
controls: route selection as the primary control: prefer waterborne e-coat + thermal sol-gel one-packs + 1K acrylic over 2K-PU-spray — this removes the isocyanate and most flammable-spray exposure at small performance cost
if 2K PU is ever adopted: brush/dip only (no spray) at DIY scale, nitrile+organic-vapor respirator, or outsource that SKU to a coating shop
LEV/extraction for any solvent spray; no ignition sources; grounded metal booth parts; flammables cabinet for lacquers/solvents/NC
UV: enclosed cure box or amber shields + gloves (acrylate skin contact discipline: nitrile, changed often — acrylates permeate)
cure oven dedicated, vented to extraction, oven thermometer audit; power-off interlock habit before reaching in
e-coat: supply on soft-start, dead-front connections, dry hands rule, tank lid when live
gloves-only handling post-clean protects BOTH the operator and the coating

waste segregation: solvent/lacquer liquid waste to flammables collection; gelled sol-gel and cured-film solids as ordinary/industrial solid per local rule; BTA/thiol dip spent baths collected as aqueous organic waste — never drained [FACT: hazard classes]; local discharge and consumer-product coating-VOC rules [UNKNOWN — needs local regulation check]
safety.waste: Smallest and mildest waste footprint in the factory: (1) flammable solvent liquids (lacquer washings, IPA) — flammables drum, licensed disposal; (2) aqueous e-coat dump and rinses — emulsion polymer, low-toxicity but high-COD, licensed disposal not drain; (3) spent azole/thiol dips — small-volume aquatic-relevant organics, collect; (4) cured-film solids, gelled sol, wipes — solid waste (NC-containing wipes: wetted storage, fire class). No heavy metals, no cyanide, no precious-metal value — nothing here goes to the reclaimer.

diy_feasibility.verdict: YES — the most DIY-compatible family in the entire factory, and the highest leverage per currency-unit: an anti-tarnish dip plus a benchtop e-coat kit turns economically thin gold into a commercially durable product, which directly serves the owner's minimum-gold-per-piece goal. The honest hierarchy for the shop: (1) molecular anti-tarnish dip on everything Ag/Cu/Ni-exposing — near-free; (2) jewelry-trade cathodic e-coat clear as the standard jewelry topcoat — mature kits, modest skills, one oven; (3) sol-gel one-pack hybrid for houseware exteriors needing max wet-applied hardness; (4) 1K acrylic (Incralac-class) for large gilded décor and anything wanting reversibility; (5) PVD nitride caps only if/when the sibling PVD line exists anyway — never bought FOR this family alone. Skip at DIY: 2K PU spray (isocyanate), nitrocellulose (fire + yellowing), chromates (prohibited).
diy_feasibility.minimum_viable_setup: ultrasonic cleaner + IPA + lint-free wipes + nitrile gloves; 1 L BTA or commercial thiol anti-tarnish dip; 1-5 L cathodic clear e-coat kit + 0-150 V/1 A DC supply + SS counter-electrode + magnetic stirrer; dedicated benchtop convection oven with independent thermometer; lidded flash-off tote (dust); pencil-hardness set, cross-hatch blade+tape, rub cloth; acetone strip jar for rework; optional: 0.3 mm airbrush + extracted spray corner for houseware lacquer, 405 nm LED cure box. [ESTIMATE: setup class, high confidence on component list, no invented prices]
diy_feasibility.hard_limits: physics/sequence: no topcoat survives post-coat forming — piece must be final-shape first, which chains this family permanently AFTER the forming step in any line layout; polymer clears cap out around 2-4H pencil and always alter feel/gloss vs bare metal — true 'invisible' scratch-proofing does not exist, the premium tier must choose between honest-thick hard gold (gold cost) and PVD cap (capex+color-match); sol-gel ceiling ~10 um/9H but glass-brittle; regulatory: EN 1811-after-EN-12472 cannot be passed BY a lacquer on an otherwise non-compliant stack [FACT: regulation structure]; food-contact clearance of any organic coat is paperwork the DIY shop cannot self-declare [UNKNOWN — needs supplier declaration + per-market rules] — design around it (food-side bare gold); aging clock: every organic clear yellows/embrittles eventually — premium positioning must either budget re-finish service or use no-topcoat routes.
